title: New Jersey Man Pleads Guilty to Shooting a French Bulldog Left in His Care
seoTitle: NJ Man Pleads Guilty to Shooting French Bulldog
description: A New Jersey man pleaded guilty on Nov 16, 2026, to shooting Ruby, a 1-year-old French Bulldog he was watching. How a necropsy exposed it, and how to choose a sitter.
secondaryKeywords: animal cruelty guilty plea New Jersey

faq.q: What happened to the French Bulldog in Berkeley Township, New Jersey?
faq.a: Ruby, a 1-year-old French Bulldog, was shot in the face on October 3, 2025, while her owner had left her in the care of Jeffrey Lentz, 57. He pleaded guilty on November 16, 2026, to animal cruelty and possession of a weapon for an unlawful purpose.

Not yet. Sentencing is set for January 22, 2027. Prosecutors will ask for five years in state prison, a concurrent three-year term for animal cruelty and a lifetime ban on owning animals; the judge decides.
A necropsy at the New Jersey Animal Health Diagnostic Laboratory in Trenton found that the wound to the dog's face came from a gunshot, and an X-ray showed a bullet in her jawbone.

faq.q: What is a necropsy for a dog?
faq.a: It is a veterinary examination after death, like an autopsy in people. If a pet dies suddenly in someone else's care and the explanation is unclear, ask your vet about one before cremation or burial.

faq.q: How can I check on my French Bulldog while someone else watches it?
faq.a: Leave a written care sheet with your vet's number, agree on daily photo or video updates, set a clear emergency rule, and try a short stay first before a long trip.
